```{r}
df <- read.csv("/Users/silkemaus/Downloads/PhD/April26/cyclo_EGU/1408_1410.csv")
```

Depth Span: 190 m Age Span: 6.39796 Myr --> 6397.96 kyr

--> SR = 190m/6.39796 Myr = 29.6970 m/Myr --> 2.97 cm/kyr

```{r}
# interpolate
series_int <- linterp(series)

```
# MTM

```{r}
TiAl_mtm <- mtm(series_int, tbw=2, ntap=3, output =1)
names(TiAl_mtm)
```
lambda = 1/f
eg. lambda = 1/0.069 = 14.39 m (i.e. Period) 
this means 1 completele oscillation every 14.39 metres

# compare to orbital cycles
1) does 10.4 m represent 100 kyr eccentricity cycle?

10.4/100 kyr = 10.4 cm/kyr (sounds plausible)

2) does 10.4m represent 20 kyr precession cycle?
10.4/20 kyr = 52. cm/kyr (doesn't make sense)

```{r}
periodogram(series_int)
```
```{r}
plot(TiAl_mtm$Frequency,
     TiAl_mtm$Power,
     type = "l",
     xlab = "Frequency (cycles/m)",
     ylab = "Power")
```

3) run ASM separately for precession, obliquity and eccentricity

```{r}
# eccentricity asm
freq_sig_ecc <- c(0.08315789, 0.09578947, 0.1073684)
TiAl_asm_ecc <- asm(freq = freq_sig_ecc,
                    target = target_ecc,
                    rayleigh = ray,
                    nyquist = nyq,
                    fper = rep(0.3, length(target_pre)),
                    numsed = 100,
                    sedmin = 3,
                    sedmax = 20,
                    iter = 500,
                    genplot = TRUE,
                    output = TRUE,
                    linLog = 1)
```
